data.narrative:
Mesh Optical Technologies is a Series A chip and semiconductor company that has raised $50M to date. Valuation triangulation draws on a peer universe of 3 private-market comparables in the same sector and stage (SambaNova Systems at $11.0B, Rebellions at $2.3B, and d-Matrix at $2.0B), alongside 3 public semiconductor benchmarks (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) though the latter cannot be applied without disclosed revenue.

Two methods yield actionable results. Stage-progression analysis, applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement to the $50M raised proxy, implies $100M. Peer-median valuation across the three same-stage, same-sector comparables yields $2.3B, with a range spanning $2.0B to $11.0B. The wide peer range reflects heterogeneity in market positioning and capital efficiency within early-stage semiconductor ventures.

Triangulation across these two methods supports a valuation range of $85M (floor) to $2.7B (ceiling), with a median point of $1.2B. The substantial gap between the stage-progression floor and peer-median midpoint reflects tension between capital-deployed benchmarking and peer trading multiples in a capital-intensive sector. Key uncertainties include technology differentiation relative to comparables, path to revenue, and whether the company's optical approach commands a premium or discount to conventional semiconductor plays.
